Asha (PM): Heads-up: customer A and B pushed back on our default quota shaping for Dedicated. They want predictable per-class throughput (embedding vs chat) inside a single reserved pool. Need product decision: expose pinned lanes or keep simple buckets?
Ravi (Eng): Pinned lanes are doable but add allocator complexity. We can implement soft-pins (best-effort %) first, then strict reservation later. Soft-pins: allocator biases scheduling but allows spill.
Mei (SRE): If we do soft-pins, we need circuit-breakers per lane to stop noisy traffic. Suggest: lane_token_bucket + emergency-throttle.
Jordan (Sales): From deals: enterprise will pay for strict reservation. They want a monthly SLA for lane minimum RPS during burst windows. Sales needs clear wording on what strict reservation means operationally.
Sam (Solutions): Customer ask: carryover unused lane capacity between billing periods for credits. Also ability to set lane_priority for mixed workloads.
Ravi (Eng): Rough config example for soft-pin MVP:
```
reserved_pool: {
  id: rp-234,
  total_tokens_per_min: 1_000_000,
  lanes: [
    {name: "chat", bias_pct: 60, burst_ceiling: 0.2},
    {name: "embed", bias_pct: 30, burst_ceiling: 0.15},
    {name: "rerank", bias_pct: 10, burst_ceiling: 0.05}
  ],
  carryover_policy: "disabled"
}
```
Ravi (Eng): For strict reservations we'd add pinned_pct and hard_admit where allocator refuses admission if lane lacks tokens. Work estimate: soft-pin = 3 weeks, strict-pin = 6-8 weeks (including tests).
Mei (SRE): Observability requirements: per-lane tail latency P95/P99, per-lane token burn rate, lane-fallback events, tenant-level preemption traces. We must surface these in Console before we offer strict SLAs.
infra-bot: Canary run queued for reserved-pools-lanes at 2024-12-01T02:00:00Z
Jordan (Sales): Also need pricing model options: a) add-on for pinned lanes, b) higher commit tier with included lane reservations, c) pay-per-burst for temporary pinning. Which path do we want to present?
Asha (PM): Product choices to decide today:
- Offer pinned lanes as "paid add-on" only at GA, keep soft-pins default for self-serve.
- Support carryover as premium feature (opt-in for contracted customers).
- Require SRE telemetry gating before any SLA-backed pinned lane is sold.
Sam (Solutions): Migration story: for customers with existing single-bucket commits, we should offer a migration tool to split commit into lanes and simulate traffic to validate. Suggest a test harness + sample terraform.
Ravi (Eng): Risk: workload classification accuracy. If customers mislabel heavy rerank jobs as embed, they'll starve other lanes. Need tagging enforcement and optional auto-classifier.
Mei (SRE): Anti-abuse: per-session max tokens + anomaly score. If burn_rate anomaly triggers, auto-demote pin for that session and alert ops.
Jordan (Sales): I'll draft three example SLA sheets (soft, pinned-add-on, strict-reserve) for legal. Need exact numbers for minimum RPS and credit formulas.
Asha (PM): Proposed acceptance criteria for GA rollout:
- Soft-pins shipped to self-serve with console controls for lane biases.
- Telemetry: per-lane metrics live, alert on burn-rate > 2x baseline.
- Pilot: one customer on strict pinned lane add-on with documented preemption rules.
- Billing: lane-level metering exported to invoice CSV.
Ravi (Eng): Action items:
- Implement allocator soft-pin bias and expose lane config in API (due: 2w).
- Add carryover toggles but default off; carryover implementation scoped to pilot (due: 6w).
Mei (SRE): Action items:
- Add lane metrics to Console and create canary alerts (due: 1w).
- Define anomaly thresholds and runbook entries (due: 1w).
Jordan (Sales) & Sam (Solutions): Action items:
- Draft SLA options + pilot sell sheet; collect customer success stories for pilot (due: 10d).
Asha (PM): We'll lock default behavior: soft-pins GA + pinned lanes as paid pilot/enterprise feature. If no objections, I'll ship the RFC for allocator changes tomorrow. Please react with :eyes: or comment by EOD.
Ravi (Eng): :eyes: logging initial perf numbers in RFC.
Mei (SRE): :eyes: will add runbook notes.
Jordan (Sales): :eyes: starting legal loop.
Sam (Solutions): :eyes: prepping migration guide template.
Asha (PM): Thanks all — keeping this thread for audit. We'll review pilot candidates in next roadmap review.
